title: Lesson 45 - I Could Use Some Advice

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I could use some advice. The arts center has asked for three extra graphics by Friday, but I only agreed to make one poster after the text and permissions are ready.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Do you want help deciding whether to do the extra work, or help deciding how to reply?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Both, really. I want to support the project, but there is no final text, no separate brief and no budget in the email.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Then you could ask Priya to separate the original poster from the new request.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: That would make the scope clearer. I'm worried that asking about money will sound unfriendly because the project is community-based.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: You might want to ask about scope, deadline and budget together. That sounds like project planning, not a demand for payment.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: True. The deadline is also difficult. I have two client files due on Thursday.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I think you should protect work that you have already promised. A volunteer request doesn't cancel a paid commitment.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: So the issue isn't whether community work matters. It's whether I can responsibly add three undefined items this week.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Exactly. I'd avoid replying with a quick yes and trying to solve the details later.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: What about refusing everything now?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: You don't have to decide that today. First ask for the missing information. If the extra work is still unrealistic, you can decline it clearly.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Let's compare the advice by risk and reversibility. Asking for a written scope is low-risk and keeps the conversation open.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: And keeping your original one-poster commitment prevents the new request from replacing what you actually agreed to.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: The downside is that Priya may still need a quick answer about Friday.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Then give her a time when you can respond after she clarifies the request. A clear next step is better than a vague maybe.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Based on that, the best fit is to ask for a separate brief today and say that I can't confirm Friday until I see the scope, deadline and budget.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: That sounds measured. Which second piece of advice are you choosing?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I'll protect the existing poster commitment and avoid promising any extra graphics until we have a separate agreement.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Good. The choice is yours, but now your reply can show both support and a real boundary.
